ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the outer boundary is square ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left. Inside the square there is a small white square, and around it are four gray congruent rectangles, arranged in a windmill shape: one horizontal rectangle above, one vertical rectangle on the right, one horizontal rectangle below, and one vertical rectangle on the left. Then reason: Let the length and width of each gray rectangle be L and W respectively. According to the arrangement in the figure, the upper side of the outer square is composed of the length L of the upper horizontal rectangle plus the width W of the right vertical rectangle, so the side length of the outer square is L+W. The perimeter of each gray rectangle is 40 cm, therefore 2(L+W)=40, obtaining L+W=20. Thus the side length of square ABCD is 20 cm, and the area is 20^2=400 cm^2.

raw_record.question_text: Square $A B C D$ is comprised of one inner square (white) and four shaded congruent rectangles. Each shaded rectangle has a perimeter of $40 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the area (in $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$) of square $A B C D$?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a pinwheel made of four congruent shaded rectangles around a central white square. Let each shaded rectangle have side lengths L and W. From the image, along the top side of the outer square, the horizontal top rectangle contributes its long side L and the thickness of the vertical right rectangle contributes W, so the side length of square ABCD is L + W. From the text, each shaded rectangle has perimeter 40, so 2(L + W) = 40 and L + W = 20. Therefore the outer square side is 20 and its area is 20^2 = 400.

method.method_draft: Use a cut-position/outer-side variable approach. Let the side length of square ABCD be s. From the image, if the common thickness of the shaded rectangles is t, then the top shaded rectangle has dimensions t by s - t: its thickness is t, and its horizontal length stops where the right shaded rectangle of width t begins. The congruent rectangles therefore all have side lengths t and s - t. From the text, each shaded rectangle has perimeter 40, so 2(t + (s - t)) = 40. This simplifies to 2s = 40, so s = 20. Hence the area of square ABCD is s^2 = 400.
